title: iPhone Duo Screens Crack at Hinge on Launch Day, Users Report Issues
body:
Apple’s latest flagship, the iPhone Duo, has hit a rocky start as a wave of early adopters report that the device’s dual‑screen hinge is developing cracks within hours of unboxing. The problem, which appears to affect the fragile glass panels that fold together, has quickly become a talking point on social media and forums, prompting concerns about quality control for the company’s most ambitious hardware venture to date. While Apple has yet to issue an official statement, the reports have already sparked a flurry of customer complaints, warranty inquiries, and speculation about the long‑term durability of foldable smartphones.

The iPhone Duo, unveiled with much fanfare as the first Apple device to feature a seamless foldable display, launched worldwide this week with pre‑orders selling out within minutes. Yet, within the first 48 hours, dozens of users have posted photos and videos showing visible fissures radiating from the hinge area, sometimes accompanied by discoloration or a faint “spider‑web” pattern across the screen. In several cases, the cracks have rendered touch input unresponsive on one side of the device, effectively turning the premium phone into a single‑screen unit. A handful of owners have already taken their phones to Apple Stores, where technicians confirmed the damage and offered replacements, but the sheer volume of reports suggests a systemic issue rather than isolated incidents.

Industry analysts point to the inherent challenges of engineering a foldable display that meets Apple’s exacting standards for both aesthetics and performance. The hinge mechanism must balance smooth operation with structural integrity, all while protecting the ultra‑thin glass from stress concentrations that can lead to micro‑fractures. Competitors such as Samsung and Huawei have faced similar hurdles in earlier generations of foldable phones, often resorting to polymer substrates or reinforced glass to mitigate breakage. Apple’s decision to use a newly developed “InfinityFlex” glass—marketed as the thinnest, most flexible glass ever produced—may have pushed the limits of current material science, leaving the hinge vulnerable during everyday opening and closing motions.

Consumer reaction has been swift and unforgiving. On platforms like Twitter, Reddit’s r/Apple community, and the Apple Support forums, users are sharing troubleshooting tips, ranging from gently “resetting” the hinge to applying temporary protective films. Some have suggested that the cracks could be a result of shipping vibrations or improper handling during the unboxing process, but many owners insist they followed the standard “unbox, power on, and start using” routine. The growing chorus of dissatisfaction has already begun to affect the Duo’s resale value, with listings on secondary markets showing a noticeable discount compared to the launch price. Moreover, the issue arrives at a delicate time for Apple, which is seeking to diversify its product lineup beyond the iPhone 15 series and cement its leadership in emerging form‑factor technologies.

Apple’s track record with hardware issues offers a mixed precedent. The company has previously navigated problems ranging from the “bendgate” controversy of the iPhone 6 to battery throttling disputes, typically responding with repair programs, software updates, or, in some cases, public apologies. Analysts expect Apple to launch a repair or replacement initiative if the hinge cracks prove to be a widespread defect, likely accompanied by a design revision for the next production run. Supply chain insiders hint that Apple may already be working on a reinforced version of the hinge, potentially delaying shipments for the second‑generation Duo slated for release later this year.

Looking ahead, the iPhone Duo’s early setbacks underscore the broader industry tension between innovation and reliability. As manufacturers race to deliver ever‑more flexible devices, the pressure to perfect new materials and mechanisms intensifies. For Apple, the immediate priority will be to reassure customers through transparent communication and swift remediation, lest the Duo’s reputation suffer lasting damage. If the company can resolve the hinge issue and refine the design, the foldable iPhone could still redefine how users interact with smartphones. However, the episode serves as a cautionary reminder that even tech giants are not immune to the growing pains of pioneering new hardware frontiers.
